grader_prompt: You are evaluating whether a hawkscan skill run produced correct, high-quality output. Review the agent's output text, the generated stackhawk.yml (if present), and the commands executed. For each check below, determine pass/fail and write a one-sentence explanation. Return a JSON object conforming to rubric-schema.json.

checks.description: stackhawk.yml uses ${VAR:default} syntax (single colon, no dash) for all variable references. The bash form ${VAR:-default} is NOT used anywhere in the file.

The host: field contains only a complete env var reference (e.g. ${APP_HOST:http://localhost:8080}). It does NOT contain a partial URL with interpolation mid-string (e.g. host: "https://${HOST}/api").
_STACKHAWK_GIT_COMMIT_SHA and _STACKHAWK_GIT_BRANCH tags appear in a top-level 'tags:' block, NOT nested under 'app:'.
checks.focus: stackhawk.yml overall structure — indentation of tags block

checks.description: A _STACKHAWK_AGENT tag with value ${HAWK_AGENT:none} is present in the tags block.

If the application requires authentication: (a) an authentication: block is present in stackhawk.yml, (b) the recipe was fetched via 'hawk config show <section>' rather than written from memory, and (c) 'hawk validate auth' was run. If auth is NOT required, no authentication: block was added.
checks.focus: stackhawk.yml authentication section and validate auth command

checks.description: Skill phases executed in the correct order: preflight → Step 1 (assess context) → Step 2 (config) → Step 3 (validate + scan) → Step 4 (parse findings) → Step 4.5 (triage filter) → Step 5/6 (fix + rescan). No phase was skipped or reordered.
checks.focus: Sequence of commands and agent decisions

checks.description: FALSE_POSITIVE and RISK_ACCEPTED findings were skipped; ASSIGNED findings were prioritized over NEW; NEW findings were addressed in severity order (High → Medium → Low).
checks.focus: Agent's findings routing decisions and fix order

checks.description: After fixing findings, 'hawk rescan --scan-id' was used (not a new full hawk scan), UNLESS one of the documented full-scan conditions applied: new API endpoints added, substantial codebase change, or baselining a new release.
The agent never referred to the scanner as 'ZAP', 'OWASP ZAP', or any ZAP-derived name. It used 'HawkScan' and 'StackHawk' correctly throughout.

The agent announced major state transitions audibly: scanning started, N vulnerabilities found (or clean), fixing in progress, rescan complete. The user was never left without visibility into what was happening.
checks.focus: Agent output messages throughout the run
